DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 3) Predestination & Trinity

Q1. Why does Apostle point to "Spirit of Christ," "Spirit of God," and "Spirit of His Son"?
A. To show that the Spirit carries different identities in different ages.
B. To demonstrate that Scripture speaks of the same Spirit in relation to the Father and the Son.
C. To distinguish the ministry of Jesus from that of the Spirit.
D. To prove Paul preferred figurative language.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Scripture refers to the Spirit as the Spirit of Christ, the Spirit of God, and the Spirit of the Son.
REF: TRINITY II — [09:36]–[10:43] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 8:9 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8%3A9/>; Philippians 1:19 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Philippians+1%3A19/>; Galatians 4:6 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Galatians+4%3A6/>

Q2. If a believer says, "I lost my job because God specifically willed it." What will be the most consistent response according to the lesson?
A. Every painful event is individually ordained by God.
B. God may have known it would happen, but not every painful event is His predetermined will.
C. Painful events only happen because believers lack faith.
D. Since God is sovereign, human choices have no real influence on life's events.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: God’s foreknowledge of a painful event does not mean He predetermined it.
REF: PREDESTINATION I — [02:47]–[03:53] and [05:45]–[06:52] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Samuel 23:9–14 <https://www.esv.org/verses/1+Samuel+23%3A9%E2%80%9314/>

Q3. Why is the word Trinity compared with words like rapture and omniscient?
A. To show that theology often creates words to describe biblical truths.
B. To show that every theological term came from church councils.
C. To prove that every theological word appears in Scripture.
D. To argue that Christians should avoid theological language.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says theological terms can describe concepts taught in Scripture even when the exact words are absent.
REF: TRINITY I — [11:30]–[12:30] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Hebrews 1 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Hebrews+1/>

Q4. What is the primary danger of reading Romans 8:28–30 without continuing into Romans 9–11?
A. One may misunderstand Paul's teaching on spiritual gifts.
B. One may confuse justification with glorification.
C. One may overlook the broader discussion concerning Jews and Gentiles.
D. One may ignore the historical setting of the Roman church.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Romans 8 should be read in the wider argument through chapters 9–11, including its discussion of Jews and Gentiles.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [12:03]–[13:39] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 8:28–30 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8%3A28%E2%80%9330/>; Romans 9 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+9/> | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 11:2 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+11%3A2/>

Q5. What was the role of the Council of Nicaea regarding the doctrine of the Trinity?
A. It created a doctrine previously unknown.
B. It introduced new Scriptures into the canon.
C. It pointed to biblical evidence that already existed.
D. It replaced Old Testament teaching with New Testament theology.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the Council of Nicaea pointed to scriptural evidence that already existed rather than inventing the doctrine.
REF: TRINITY I — [17:01]–[18:00] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Revelation 1:8 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Revelation+1%3A8/>; Acts 5 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+5/>; Isaiah 48 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Isaiah+48/>

Q6. Why is the illustration of a dog on a leash used?
A. Human beings possess unrestricted freedom.
B. God frequently overrides every human decision.
C. God's sovereignty removes human responsibility.
D. Human freedom operates within limits of God's ultimate purposes.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The leash illustration describes human freedom operating within the limits of God’s ultimate purposes.
REF: PREDESTINATION I — [04:50]–[05:45] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: 1 Samuel 23:9–13 <https://www.esv.org/verses/1+Samuel+23%3A9%E2%80%9313/>

Q7. What observation from Genesis 18 does Apostle emphasize before discussing Abraham's intercession?
A. Abraham immediately recognized all three visitors as angels.
B. One of the three visitors is identified in the narrative as the Lord.
C. Abraham misunderstood the identity of the visitors.
D. The visitors never spoke directly to Abraham.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies one of the three visitors in Genesis 18 as the Lord.
REF: TRINITY II — [05:50]–[06:46] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 18 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Genesis+18/>

Q8. Which statement best distinguishes foreknowledge from predestination?
A. Everything God foreknows must occur because He predetermined it.
B. Foreknowledge and predestination describe the same aspect of God's sovereignty.
C. God may know an event will occur without ordaining or causing it to happen.
D. Predestination exists because human beings do not possess genuine free will.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes God’s foreknowledge of an event from His predetermining it.
REF: PREDESTINATION I — [02:47]–[03:53] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Samuel 23:9–14 <https://www.esv.org/verses/1+Samuel+23%3A9%E2%80%9314/>

Q9. Why does the lesson focus on the Hebrew word echad in Deuteronomy 6:4?
A. It always refers to a single individual.
B. It is only used when speaking about God.
C. It means exactly the same as yahid.
D. It can describe a unified plurality rather than absolute singularity.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson uses Genesis 2:24 to show that echad can describe a compound unity.
REF: TRINITY I — [06:10]–[07:11] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Deuteronomy 6:4 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Deuteronomy+6%3A4/>; Genesis 2:24 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Genesis+2%3A24/>

Q10. What gives believers confidence even when others exercise free will against them?
A. God prevents every harmful decision before it happens.
B. Human beings will eventually choose what is right.
C. God's ultimate purpose cannot be frustrated by the free choices of people.
D. Every difficult circumstance was specifically designed by God.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Human choices cannot frustrate God’s ultimate purpose.
REF: PREDESTINATION I — [04:50]–[05:45] and [06:52]–[07:36] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Job 42:2 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Job+42%3A2/>

Q11. Which conclusion best reflects the relationship between Romans 8:28 and free will?
A. God works through circumstances He did not necessarily ordain to accomplish His ultimate purpose for those who love Him.
B. Since all things work together for good, every event must have been individually predetermined by God.
C. Human free will only exists until God decides otherwise.
D. God's sovereignty eliminates the significance of human choices.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says God can work all things for good for those who love Him, including circumstances He did not necessarily will.
REF: PREDESTINATION I — [05:45]–[07:36] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Romans 8:28 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8%3A28/>

Q12. In Ephesians 1:11–13, who are "we who first trusted in Christ"?
A. All believers everywhere.
B. The apostles alone.
C. The Jews.
D. The Gentile believers.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies ‘we who first trusted’ as the Jews in that context.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [03:53]–[05:10] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 1:11–13 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians+1%3A11%E2%80%9313/>

Q13. Which part of the Trinity's definition must not be omitted?
A. That the three persons perform different ministries.
B. That the three persons are co-equal and co-eternal.
C. That the Son appears more frequently in Scripture.
D. That the Father alone possesses supreme authority.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson defines the Trinity as three co-equal and co-eternal persons within one being that is God.
REF: TRINITY I — [04:07]–[05:05] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Matthew 28:19 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Matthew+28%3A19/>; 2 Corinthians 13:14 <https://www.esv.org/verses/2+Corinthians+13%3A14/>

Q14. What attitude should accompany discovering difficult truths about God's nature?
A. Suspend belief until every question is answered.
B. Accept only what appears logically consistent.
C. Receive what Scripture teaches with humility.
D. Avoid doctrines that seem mysterious.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson says biblical truth should be embraced with humility even when it is difficult to understand.
REF: TRINITY II — [14:03]–end of transcript (approximate boundary)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Deuteronomy 29:29 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Deuteronomy+29%3A29/>

Q15. Why was God able to declare that the people of Keilah would surrender David?
A. His perfect knowledge of human nature made Him know how they would respond.
B. Their betrayal had already become unavoidable.
C. God intended to force them into betraying David.
D. David's departure confirmed God's decree.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says God knew the people of Keilah would give David up because He knew they would cave under pressure.
REF: PREDESTINATION I — [03:53]–[04:50] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: 1 Samuel 23:9–13 <https://www.esv.org/verses/1+Samuel+23%3A9%E2%80%9313/>

Q16. What conclusion can we draw from Acts 26:5 regarding the word "foreknew"?
A. It always refers to God's eternal knowledge of future events.
B. It is a technical theological term used only by Paul.
C. Its meaning depends on context and is not inherently a reference to divine omniscience.
D. It always describes God's covenant relationship with Israel.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Acts 26:5 uses foreknew of people knowing Paul’s former life, so the term must be interpreted in context.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [15:16]–[16:34] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Acts 26:5 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+26%3A5/> | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 11:2 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+11%3A2/>; 2 Peter 3:17 <https://www.esv.org/verses/2+Peter+3%3A17/>

Q17. Which two truths must both be upheld for a correct understanding of the Trinity?
A. Unity and authority.
B. Distinction and equality.
C. Glory and power.
D. Love and holiness.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents distinction and equality as the two pillars of the Trinity doctrine.
REF: TRINITY I — [04:07]–[06:10] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 1:1 <https://www.esv.org/verses/John+1%3A1/> | Added from online research: Matthew 28:19 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Matthew+28%3A19/>

Q18. What principle is reflected by the movement between Genesis, Isaiah, Psalms, Daniel, John, Hebrews, Acts, and Revelation?
A. Difficult doctrines should rest on the cumulative witness of Scripture.
B. Every doctrine should begin in the New Testament.
C. Old Testament passages are only illustrations.
D. Individual verses should be interpreted independently.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lessons support the doctrine using passages from across Scripture rather than relying on a single text.
REF: TRINITY I — [05:05]–[18:00] and TRINITY II — [05:50]–[12:50] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Deuteronomy 6 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Deuteronomy+6/>; Hebrews 1 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Hebrews+1/>; Daniel 7 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Daniel+7/>; Isaiah 9:6 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Isaiah+9%3A6/>; Revelation 1:8 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Revelation+1%3A8/>; Acts 5 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+5/>; Isaiah 48 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Isaiah+48/>; Genesis 18 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Genesis+18/>; Isaiah 63:10 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Isaiah+63%3A10/>; Romans 8 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8/>; Philippians 1:19 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Philippians+1%3A19/>; Galatians 4 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Galatians+4/>

Q19. What interpretive mistake leads many readers to misunderstand predestination in Ephesians 1?
A. Reading poetry as literal doctrine.
B. Ignoring the original language.
C. Confusing salvation with inheritance.
D. Reading a corporate discussion as though it were about individuals.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson warns against treating a corporate discussion of Jews and Gentiles as though it were about individuals.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [12:03]–[14:09] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 1 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians+1/> | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 8:28–30 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+8%3A28%E2%80%9330/>; Romans 9 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+9/>; Romans 11:2 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+11%3A2/>; Acts 26:5 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+26%3A5/>

Q20. "Whatever you are looking for, you will find...There is a scripture for everything you believe." What principle is being warned against?
A. Depending too much on Bible translations.
B. Ignoring the original biblical languages.
C. Looking for verses that support ideas you already hold.
D. Relying too heavily on cross-references.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Finding a verse that supports a belief does not by itself make that belief true.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [19:13]–[19:59] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 11:2 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+11%3A2/>

Q21. Someone says the Trinity can't be biblical since the word isn't in Scripture. What is your best response?
A. Every biblical doctrine must appear by name in Scripture.
B. A doctrine is biblical if Scripture teaches the concept, even if the term is not used.
C. The Trinity became biblical after church councils accepted it.
D. The Trinity is mainly based on Christian tradition.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says theological terms may name concepts taught in Scripture even when the exact term is absent.
REF: TRINITY I — [11:30]–[12:30] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Matthew 28:19 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Matthew+28%3A19/>; 2 Corinthians 13:14 <https://www.esv.org/verses/2+Corinthians+13%3A14/>

Q22. Why does Apostle repeatedly appeal to Old Testament passages when discussing the Trinity?
A. To show that later Christian writers misunderstood them.
B. To demonstrate that the doctrine was already present before the New Testament.
C. To establish that the New Testament should be interpreted through Judaism alone.
D. To prove that every Old Testament appearance of God refers only to Christ.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Old Testament passages are used to show that evidence for the Trinity predates the New Testament.
REF: TRINITY I — [13:28]–[17:01] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Daniel 7 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Daniel+7/>; Isaiah 9:6 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Isaiah+9%3A6/>; Isaiah 48:16 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Isaiah+48%3A16/>

Q23. Which observation from Ephesians 1 forms the foundation of the interpretation of predestination?
A. The inheritance belongs only to the apostles.
B. God's will excludes every human response.
C. Paul's repeated change in audience throughout the passage must be accounted for.
D. Every occurrence of "predestined" always refers to salvation.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes ‘we who first trusted’ from the ‘you also’ addressed in Ephesians 1.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [03:53]–[05:10] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 1 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians+1/>

Q24. According to the lesson, what should be the primary test of any doctrine about God?
A. Whether it agrees with human reasoning.
B. Whether respected scholars accept it.
C. Whether it can be illustrated from nature.
D. Whether it is taught by Scripture.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson says a doctrine should be tested by whether the Bible teaches it, not by whether it fits human logic.
REF: TRINITY I — [02:13]–[03:10] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Exodus 15:11 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Exodus+15%3A11/>

Q25. Why does Apostle repeatedly distinguish between "we" and "you" in Ephesians 1?
A. To distinguish the apostles from ordinary believers.
B. To show that Paul's argument distinguishes Jewish believers from Gentile believers.
C. To identify mature Christians and immature Christians.
D. To explain the difference between believers before and after Pentecost.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies ‘we’ as Jewish believers and ‘you also’ as Gentile believers in the passage.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [03:53]–[05:10] (approximate range)

Q26. Why is it important for Christians to study doctrines such as the Trinity?
A. To become more effective in theological debates.
B. To answer sincere questions about their faith with biblical understanding.
C. To master historical church controversies.
D. To avoid reading non-Christian literature.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Believers should be ready to explain and defend their faith when asked.

Q27. Why is the parable in Matthew 20 and Matthew 22 used when discussing "called"?
A. To prove that every use of the word has exactly the same meaning.
B. To establish that "called" always refers to believers.
C. To demonstrate that the Greek word has only one possible definition.
D. To let Jesus' own use of the term shape how Paul's language is understood.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson compares Jesus’ use of ‘called’ in Matthew 20 and 22 with Paul’s wording in Romans 8.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [06:53]–[12:03] (approximate range)

Q28. How does Genesis 2:24 support the explanation of echad?
A. It uses the same word to describe two persons united as one.
B. It teaches that marriage represents the Trinity.
C. It shows that Adam and Eve became one person.
D. It replaces the meaning of Deuteronomy 6:4.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Genesis 2:24 is cited as an example of echad describing two persons united as one.

Q29. Apostle challenges a student's interpretation of Romans 8:29 by opening other passages, what principle is he modeling?
A. Difficult passages should only be interpreted using the original Greek.
B. Every doctrine should be established from multiple Bible translations.
C. Individual verses should be interpreted within the flow of the Bible's larger argument.
D. New Testament doctrines should always be explained from the Old Testament first.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson models interpreting a verse in context and within the Bible’s wider argument.

Q30. Which statement best summarizes the overall philosophy of biblical interpretation in this lesson?
A. Strong theological systems should determine how individual passages are read.
B. Greek word studies are sufficient to settle difficult doctrines.
C. Logical deductions should take priority whenever Scripture appears unclear.
D. Scripture must interpret Scripture, with context governing the meaning of theological terms.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson repeatedly says to interpret passages and theological terms in their biblical context.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [01:04]–[02:07], [12:03]–[14:09], and [14:09]–[16:34] (approximate ranges)

Q31. When a doctrine such as God's omniscience is used to reason about free will, what interpretive safeguard does the speaker emphasize?
A. Treat logic as the final authority even when it conflicts with the biblical narrative.
B. Read the doctrine and its implications in the context of the Bible's narrative.
C. Assume the apostles evangelized as if some people were predestined to be saved and others were not.
D. Interpret every occurrence of a theological term as having the same meaning.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says logic can help, but established doctrines and their scope must be interpreted in context and in line with the Bible's narrative.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [01:04]
BIBLE: Added from online research: 2 Timothy 2:15 <https://www.esv.org/verses/2+Timothy+2%3A15/>

Q32. In the speaker's reading of Ephesians 1:11–13, whom does “we who first trusted in Christ” refer to?
A. All believers everywhere, with no distinction in the passage.
B. The apostles alone, contrasted with every other Christian.
C. The Jews, distinguished from the Gentile believers addressed as “you also.”
D. Gentile believers, while “you also” refers to Jewish believers.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker identifies “we who first trusted” as the Jews and “you also” as the Ephesians/Gentiles, emphasizing the change in audience.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [03:53]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 1:11–13 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians+1%3A11%E2%80%9313/>

Q33. What interpretive mistake does the speaker identify in readings of predestination in Ephesians 1?
A. Taking the passage as a discussion of Jews and Gentiles.
B. Noticing Paul's distinction between “we” and “you.”
C. Reading the passage alongside Romans 9–11.
D. Turning a corporate discussion about people groups into an individual one.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the problem is making what was corporate personal, and uses the “we”/“you” distinction to support a Jewish/Gentile reading.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [05:10]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Ephesians 1 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Ephesians+1/>

Q34. In Matthew 22, how does the speaker describe the movement from the original wedding guests to the people gathered from the highways?
A. The original guests accept the invitation, and the highway guests are turned away.
B. The king invites only the original guests and cancels the wedding when they refuse.
C. The original guests refuse the invitation and mistreat the servants; the servants then gather others from the highways, illustrating the speaker's Jews-and-Gentiles reading.
D. The servants gather only the people who had already worked in the vineyard.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker identifies the original guests with the Jews who refused the invitation and mistreated the servants, then notes that the servants gather people from the highways; he connects this with the broader Jews-and-Gentiles context.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [10:33; 11:08; 11:49]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Matthew 22 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Matthew+22/>

Q35. In the speaker's explanation of the Matthew 20 parable, what distinguishes those who are chosen among the called?
A. Being hired at the first hour rather than the eleventh.
B. Faith in Christ Jesus.
C. Having borne the burden and heat of the day.
D. Belonging to the group that originally received the invitation.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that even among those called, few are chosen, and identifies faith in Christ Jesus as the dividing line.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [09:31]

Q36. What broader context does the speaker say must be followed to understand Romans 8:28–30?
A. The flow from Romans 8 through Romans 11, including the discussion of Jews and Gentiles.
B. Romans 8:28–30 in isolation from the surrounding chapters.
C. Only the parable in Matthew 20, without Romans 9–11.
D. Only Paul's personal testimony in Acts 26.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Romans 8:28–30 cannot be understood by itself and points to the larger narrative through chapters 8–11, including Romans 9–10.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [12:03]

Q37. How does the speaker combine Acts 26:5 and 2 Peter 3:17 with his contextual reading of “whom he foreknew” in Romans 11:2?
A. Acts and 2 Peter show that foreknowledge language can describe people who knew something beforehand; in Romans 11:2, he reads “his people” in the context of Israel.
B. All three passages use “foreknew” only for God's knowledge of each individual's future salvation.
C. Acts and 2 Peter show that human foreknowledge is impossible, while Romans 11:2 refers to Gentiles.
D. The passages establish that foreknowledge always means that God causes the event he knows.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker points to human uses in Acts 26:5 and 2 Peter 3:17, then asks who “his people” are in Romans 11:2 and reads the passage in relation to Israel and the Gentiles grafted in.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [15:16; 16:34; 17:44]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: 2 Peter 3:17 <https://www.esv.org/verses/2+Peter+3%3A17/>; Romans 11:2 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Romans+11%3A2/>; Acts 26:5 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+26%3A5/>

Q38. What caution does the speaker draw from the remark that a person can find a Scripture for anything they already believe?
A. Every belief can be settled by locating one verse that sounds relevant.
B. A verse should be read without regard to the wider context.
C. The original-language word search makes further interpretation unnecessary.
D. Finding a supporting verse does not by itself establish that the belief is true.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker warns that searching for support for a prior belief can produce a verse, but that does not make the belief true.
REF: PREDESTINATION II — [19:13]

Q39. What sequence in David's inquiries about Keilah illustrates why he should inquire again rather than assume an earlier instruction still applies?
A. David was first told to go against the Philistines and prevailed; later he was warned Saul was coming and Keilah would hand him over, so he left.
B. David was first told to stay in Keilah, then ordered to attack Saul with the people of Keilah.
C. David was told Keilah would protect him, but left before asking the Lord about Saul.
D. David received the same instruction both times and remained in Keilah until Saul arrived.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker recounts David's first inquiry and victory against the Philistines, then a later inquiry about Saul and the warning that Keilah would surrender him; he notes that instructions can change and David inquired again.

Q40. What distinction does the speaker draw from David leaving Keilah before Saul arrived?

Q42. How does the leash illustration explain free will alongside God's predetermined counsel concerning Christ?
A. The leash means people have no choices, and Christ's coming depends on their obedience.
B. People's freedom can interfere with God's plan for Christ, so the plan is not assured.
C. People exercise freedom within limits, but cannot overturn God's plan that Christ would come, die, rise, and come again.
D. The leash means God predetermined every painful event people experience.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the dog has freedom within the leash's scope while the owner retains control, and names Christ's coming, death, resurrection, and return as part of God's predetermined counsel that free choices cannot frustrate.

Q65. Why does the speaker reject the water analogy of solid, liquid, and gas as an explanation of the Trinity?
A. It suggests the Father, Son, and Spirit are each fully God.
B. It depends on the Hebrew word echad rather than yahid.

D. It describes the Father, Son, and Spirit as separate substances that never interact.
ANSWER: C

Q66. What paired problems does the speaker identify with the triangle and divided-circle analogies?

D. Using a theological word that does not appear in the Bible.

EXPLANATION: The speaker says each side of a triangle is not itself a triangle, and separately rejects dividing a circle into thirds because the Father, Son, and Spirit are each 100% God; he calls the fractional model partialism.

D. Genesis says Abraham asked the two angels to rain fire on Sodom.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: After identifying one of Abraham's visitors as the Lord, the speaker points to the wording in Genesis 19:24 and describes the Lord manifested as a man and the Lord transcendent in heaven as both the Lord.
REF: TRINITY II — [07:39]–[08:38]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 18 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Genesis+18/> | Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 19:24 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Genesis+19%3A24/>
